title: Learned bubble reconstruction shows focus-dependent distribution agreement
summary: A convolutional multitask model trained on simulated optical images was applied without experimental fine-tuning to bubble shadowgraphs at four radial planes. Reconstructed size distributions overlapped in-focus experimental references by approximately 68–92%, with poorer agreement farther from the focal reference. This is a configuration-specific population measurement validation; experimental three-dimensional coordinates were not independently known for each bubble.

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, computational Methods, application Results and limitations; no independent reproduction

evidence.tested: The model jointly predicts depth relative to the known focal plane and physical-equivalent diameter. Experimental populations contained 142, 971, 859 and 204 reconstructed bubbles; distributions were compared with plane-specific in-focus references. A separate 11,679-bubble center-plane reference comparison is reported.
evidence.unknown: The 97.6% normalized depth accuracy belongs to synthetic data, not experimental depth truth. Model training describes a randomized crop development split alongside a timestamp-separated test; these partitions should not be conflated. Experimental references are distribution-level and share the imaging facility. Center-reference comparisons use differing summaries (approximately 92% versus 86% overlap); no single pooled value is inferred. Optical configuration, segmentation, overlap and defocus limit transfer; no general three-dimensional accuracy or improved flow process was established.
evidence.ai_role: A learned convolutional appearance representation, conditioned on focal-plane position, jointly infers size and depth from optical signatures and enables the scoped distribution-level reference comparison.
